segments.text: Quinn Steele, Planning Commission staff. Ta/cpa 26-05, which is a map amendment for 3541 North Boulevard. The request before you is privately initiated and small scale covering approximately 1.34 acres. The request is to go from public/semi-public to the residential 3 future land use designation. Here is a general location map. The subject site is located within the central Tampa Planning district, the Tampa Heights urban village and the Tampa Heights neighborhood. Here is an aerial photo of the subject site which is outlined in yellow along North Boulevard. Historically, the property was owned by the City of Tampa and was sold to the greater showmen's association in 1971. The parcel is currently under private ownership. Properties east of the red dashed lines are within the Tampa Heights urban village, while properties west of the line are outside of the urban village and primarily developed with single-family detached homes. Immediately north of the site is the showmen's rest cemetery. While beth Israel cemetery and woodlawn cemetery are located to the east and south. There is a Place of Religious Assembly located at the southern portion of the block. Additional, calvin Taylor park is located to the northeast and plymouth playground is located to the southeast. This is a photo looking west on the subject site towards North Boulevard. A photo looking south at the subject site, North Boulevard is out of frame to the right. The showmen's rest cemetery is behind the camera. Looking east at the subject site in the adjacent showmen's rest cemetery from North Boulevard, looking across West North Boulevard from the subject site, and looking on west North Indiana Avenue, which is one block north of the subject site. This map shows the adopted future land use as public/semi-public in blue. Showmen's rest cemetery and beth Israel cemetery to the north and east as well as the church to the south are also designated public/semi-public. Woodlawn cemetery as well as calvin Taylor park and plymouth playground are designated recreation open space in green. Properties of West North Boulevard are primarily designated residential 10. This map shows the proposed future land use as residential 3 in yellow. R 3 is one of the lowest residential density categories in the comprehensive plan at a maximum density of three dwelling units per acre. Under the existing public/semi-public designation there are no defined maximums for residential or nonresidential development. It is determined by compatibility with the surrounding area. Under the proposed r-3 designation, the site can be considered for up to four dwelling units, neighborhood, office and commercial uses would not be permitted, although certain uses such as day cares and churches could be considered at a maximum of just over 20,000 square feet. The proposed amendment would introduce a low density residential development pattern and public, quasi-public uses would no longer be required on the site. We sent this out for agency review, and the City of Tampa had an objection. City staff finds that the long-term Planning vision of the city favors a more conservative, thoughtful approach to the development around cemetery uses, which is better accommodated under the adopted p/sp future land use designation. While formulating a recommendation, Planning Commission staff reviews all related policies regarding the proposed request as discussed in the staff report, applicant submitted a dpr study that concluded that graves are not likely present on the subject site. If any potential burial resources are identified in the future, they would be addressed through subsequent development review and permitting processes. Planning Commission found this request consistent with the following objectives and policies of the comprehensive plan. First compatibility with the surrounding area. The proposed r 3 designation would introduce a low density residential development pattern that is lower density than the surrounding r-10 designation. This request would also promote infill development by providing an opportunity for residential development on undeveloped parcel within the Tampa Heights urban village. Lastly ensuring an adequate supply of housing, the proposed amendment would support additional housing opportunities by allowing limited residential development at a maximum density of three dwelling units per acre. Planning Commission recommends that the proposed map amendment be found consistent with the goals, objectives, and policies of the Tampa Comprehensive Plan, and I'm available for any questions.
